title: Housing And Tenancy — Level 1 application
question: Complete the supplied Level 1 reading lesson and independent task on housing and tenancy.
evidence_task: Formative Level 1 evidence opportunity for R1.1: retain learner work or tutor observation notes from the supplied independent task. Record support and next teaching point. This is course evidence, not the awarding organisation's live assessment.
evidence_status: Formative/internal Brainy Elephant course evidence only. The regulated assessment is externally set by Gateway Qualifications and must be administered under the current approved-centre requirements.
criterion_focus: Identify the purpose and intended audience of a range of straightforward texts
learn: Teach and model the Level 1 skill: Identify the purpose and intended audience of a range of straightforward texts. Use housing and tenancy to develop independence, accuracy, reasoning and language appropriate to purpose and audience. Stage 1: consolidate Level 1 and establish Level 1 independence.

tutor_review: Record achieved / developing / revisit against R1.1. Note accuracy, independence, reasoning and support. Keep course evidence separate from Gateway's live controlled assessment/written examination.
resources: Supplied Level 1 teaching and independent resources on housing and tenancy; learner evidence record; dictionary/reference material where permitted in teaching; writing or discussion materials.

Identify the purpose and intended audience of a range of straightforward texts.
Apply the skill independently, justify choices where appropriate and review accuracy.
key_language: purpose, audience, viewpoint, implication, evidence, contrast, however, although, therefore, relevant, infer
learner_material:
INFORMATION ARTICLE — Housing And Tenancy

A local organisation has reviewed the way it manages housing and tenancy. The changes were introduced after users reported that the previous system was difficult to understand and sometimes caused unnecessary delays. From next month, information will be available through both an online service and a staffed reception point.

The organisation says the new arrangements should make the process quicker. However, some users are concerned that people with limited digital access may still need additional support. Staff have therefore been asked to explain the options clearly and to record recurring problems so that the service can be reviewed again after three months.

Anyone affected by the changes is advised to check current guidance before making an appointment.
practice_tasks: Identify purpose, audience and text type.
Summarise the main point and supporting ideas.
Extract at least five precise details.
Explain one implied meaning or reasonable inference.
Analyse one organisational/language feature or viewpoint and explain its effect.
independent_task: Read the supplied Level 1 text independently. Answer questions on purpose, main ideas, detailed information, vocabulary/context and at least one inference or viewpoint.
success_check: Performance is relevant to R1.1 at Level 1.
Learner handles main meaning, relevant detail and appropriate language with substantial independence.
Tutor records accuracy, independence and a specific next step.
independent_resource:
INDEPENDENT READING — Housing And Tenancy

Following a six-week trial, the service has decided to continue its revised arrangements. Most users said that waiting times had improved, although several respondents wanted clearer written instructions. Managers have agreed to rewrite the guidance and provide a telephone option for people who cannot use the online system.

The next review will compare waiting times, complaints and user feedback. If the figures do not improve, further changes may be introduced. Users are encouraged to keep copies of important messages and report difficulties promptly.

learner_material:
SPOKEN MODEL — Housing And Tenancy

A: I'd like to clarify the procedure because the written instructions seem to give two different options.
B: Which part is unclear?
A: The first section says I should apply online, whereas the final paragraph says I can make an appointment. I don't have reliable internet access, so I'd prefer to speak to someone in person.
B: In that case, you can book an appointment. You'll need to bring identification and the reference letter.
A: So, just to confirm, I don't need to complete the online form first?
B: That's correct. Bring those two documents and explain the situation when you arrive.

INFORMATION ARTICLE — Environmental Issues

A local organisation has reviewed the way it manages environmental issues. The changes were introduced after users reported that the previous system was difficult to understand and sometimes caused unnecessary delays. From next month, information will be available through both an online service and a staffed reception point.

The organisation says the new arrangements should make the process quicker. However, some users are concerned that people with limited digital access may still need additional support. Staff have therefore been asked to explain the options clearly and to record recurring problems so that the service can be reviewed again after three months.

Anyone affected by the changes is advised to check current guidance before making an appointment.

INFORMATION ARTICLE — Problem Solving At Work

A local organisation has reviewed the way it manages problem solving at work. The changes were introduced after users reported that the previous system was difficult to understand and sometimes caused unnecessary delays. From next month, information will be available through both an online service and a staffed reception point.

The organisation says the new arrangements should make the process quicker. However, some users are concerned that people with limited digital access may still need additional support. Staff have therefore been asked to explain the options clearly and to record recurring problems so that the service can be reviewed again after three months.

Anyone affected by the changes is advised to check current guidance before making an appointment.

A: I'd like to clarify the procedure because the written instructions seem to give two different options.
B: Which part is unclear?
A: The first section says I should apply online, whereas the final paragraph says I can make an appointment. I don't have reliable internet access, so I'd prefer to speak to someone in person.
B: In that case, you can book an appointment. You'll need to bring identification and the reference letter.

learner_material:
INFORMATION ARTICLE — Consumer Issues

A local organisation has reviewed the way it manages consumer issues. The changes were introduced after users reported that the previous system was difficult to understand and sometimes caused unnecessary delays. From next month, information will be available through both an online service and a staffed reception point.

The organisation says the new arrangements should make the process quicker. However, some users are concerned that people with limited digital access may still need additional support. Staff have therefore been asked to explain the options clearly and to record recurring problems so that the service can be reviewed again after three months.

Anyone affected by the changes is advised to check current guidance before making an appointment.

INDEPENDENT READING — Consumer Issues

Following a six-week trial, the service has decided to continue its revised arrangements. Most users said that waiting times had improved, although several respondents wanted clearer written instructions. Managers have agreed to rewrite the guidance and provide a telephone option for people who cannot use the online system.

The next review will compare waiting times, complaints and user feedback. If the figures do not improve, further changes may be introduced. Users are encouraged to keep copies of important messages and report difficulties promptly.

learner_material:
INFORMATION ARTICLE — Digital Services

A local organisation has reviewed the way it manages digital services. The changes were introduced after users reported that the previous system was difficult to understand and sometimes caused unnecessary delays. From next month, information will be available through both an online service and a staffed reception point.

The organisation says the new arrangements should make the process quicker. However, some users are concerned that people with limited digital access may still need additional support. Staff have therefore been asked to explain the options clearly and to record recurring problems so that the service can be reviewed again after three months.

Anyone affected by the changes is advised to check current guidance before making an appointment.
practice_tasks: Identify purpose, audience and text type.
Summarise the main point and supporting ideas.
Extract at least five precise details.
Explain one implied meaning or reasonable inference.
Analyse one organisational/language feature or viewpoint and explain its effect.
independent_task: Read the supplied Level 1 text independently. Answer questions on purpose, main ideas, detailed information, vocabulary/context and at least one inference or viewpoint.
success_check: Performance is relevant to R1.7 at Level 1.
Learner handles main meaning, relevant detail and appropriate language with substantial independence.
Tutor records accuracy, independence and a specific next step.
independent_resource:
INDEPENDENT READING — Digital Services

Following a six-week trial, the service has decided to continue its revised arrangements. Most users said that waiting times had improved, although several respondents wanted clearer written instructions. Managers have agreed to rewrite the guidance and provide a telephone option for people who cannot use the online system.

The next review will compare waiting times, complaints and user feedback. If the figures do not improve, further changes may be introduced. Users are encouraged to keep copies of important messages and report difficulties promptly.

learner_material:
MODEL FORMAL MESSAGE

Dear Service Manager,

I am writing regarding rights and responsibilities. I contacted the service last week because I needed clarification about the new procedure. Although the member of staff was helpful, the written information did not explain what evidence I was expected to provide.

Could you confirm which documents are required and whether copies are acceptable? I would also suggest adding this information to the guidance, as it may prevent similar confusion for other users.

I would appreciate a response before my appointment next Tuesday.

Yours sincerely,
Alex Morgan

INDEPENDENT WRITING TASK — Rights And Responsibilities

Write approximately 100–140 words for a realistic audience. Explain a situation or issue, organise the information into logical paragraphs, give relevant detail and reasons, and state clearly what action, response or outcome you want. Use an appropriate register and format. Before finishing, edit sentence structure, tense, punctuation, spelling and vocabulary.

SPOKEN MODEL — Consumer Issues

A: I'd like to clarify the procedure because the written instructions seem to give two different options.
B: Which part is unclear?
A: The first section says I should apply online, whereas the final paragraph says I can make an appointment. I don't have reliable internet access, so I'd prefer to speak to someone in person.
B: In that case, you can book an appointment. You'll need to bring identification and the reference letter.
A: So, just to confirm, I don't need to complete the online form first?
B: That's correct. Bring those two documents and explain the situation when you arrive.

learner_material:
INFORMATION ARTICLE — Problem Solving At Work

A local organisation has reviewed the way it manages problem solving at work. The changes were introduced after users reported that the previous system was difficult to understand and sometimes caused unnecessary delays. From next month, information will be available through both an online service and a staffed reception point.

The organisation says the new arrangements should make the process quicker. However, some users are concerned that people with limited digital access may still need additional support. Staff have therefore been asked to explain the options clearly and to record recurring problems so that the service can be reviewed again after three months.

Anyone affected by the changes is advised to check current guidance before making an appointment.

INDEPENDENT READING — Problem Solving At Work

Following a six-week trial, the service has decided to continue its revised arrangements. Most users said that waiting times had improved, although several respondents wanted clearer written instructions. Managers have agreed to rewrite the guidance and provide a telephone option for people who cannot use the online system.

The next review will compare waiting times, complaints and user feedback. If the figures do not improve, further changes may be introduced. Users are encouraged to keep copies of important messages and report difficulties promptly.

learner_material:
SPOKEN MODEL — Problem Solving At Work

A: I'd like to clarify the procedure because the written instructions seem to give two different options.
B: Which part is unclear?
A: The first section says I should apply online, whereas the final paragraph says I can make an appointment. I don't have reliable internet access, so I'd prefer to speak to someone in person.
B: In that case, you can book an appointment. You'll need to bring identification and the reference letter.
A: So, just to confirm, I don't need to complete the online form first?
B: That's correct. Bring those two documents and explain the situation when you arrive.

INFORMATION ARTICLE — Community Projects

A local organisation has reviewed the way it manages community projects. The changes were introduced after users reported that the previous system was difficult to understand and sometimes caused unnecessary delays. From next month, information will be available through both an online service and a staffed reception point.

The organisation says the new arrangements should make the process quicker. However, some users are concerned that people with limited digital access may still need additional support. Staff have therefore been asked to explain the options clearly and to record recurring problems so that the service can be reviewed again after three months.

Anyone affected by the changes is advised to check current guidance before making an appointment.

Dear Service Manager,

I am writing regarding formal appointments. I contacted the service last week because I needed clarification about the new procedure. Although the member of staff was helpful, the written information did not explain what evidence I was expected to provide.

Yours sincerely,
Alex Morgan

SPOKEN MODEL — Community Projects

A: I'd like to clarify the procedure because the written instructions seem to give two different options.
B: Which part is unclear?
A: The first section says I should apply online, whereas the final paragraph says I can make an appointment. I don't have reliable internet access, so I'd prefer to speak to someone in person.
B: In that case, you can book an appointment. You'll need to bring identification and the reference letter.
A: So, just to confirm, I don't need to complete the online form first?
B: That's correct. Bring those two documents and explain the situation when you arrive.

learner_material:
INFORMATION ARTICLE — Complaints And Resolutions

A local organisation has reviewed the way it manages complaints and resolutions. The changes were introduced after users reported that the previous system was difficult to understand and sometimes caused unnecessary delays. From next month, information will be available through both an online service and a staffed reception point.

The organisation says the new arrangements should make the process quicker. However, some users are concerned that people with limited digital access may still need additional support. Staff have therefore been asked to explain the options clearly and to record recurring problems so that the service can be reviewed again after three months.

Anyone affected by the changes is advised to check current guidance before making an appointment.

learner_material:
INFORMATION ARTICLE — Travel Disruption

A local organisation has reviewed the way it manages travel disruption. The changes were introduced after users reported that the previous system was difficult to understand and sometimes caused unnecessary delays. From next month, information will be available through both an online service and a staffed reception point.

The organisation says the new arrangements should make the process quicker. However, some users are concerned that people with limited digital access may still need additional support. Staff have therefore been asked to explain the options clearly and to record recurring problems so that the service can be reviewed again after three months.

Anyone affected by the changes is advised to check current guidance before making an appointment.

success_check: Performance is relevant to R1.1 at Level 1.
Learner handles main meaning, relevant detail and appropriate language with substantial independence.
Tutor records accuracy, independence and a specific next step.
independent_resource:
INDEPENDENT READING — Travel Disruption

Following a six-week trial, the service has decided to continue its revised arrangements. Most users said that waiting times had improved, although several respondents wanted clearer written instructions. Managers have agreed to rewrite the guidance and provide a telephone option for people who cannot use the online system.

The next review will compare waiting times, complaints and user feedback. If the figures do not improve, further changes may be introduced. Users are encouraged to keep copies of important messages and report difficulties promptly.

Alex Morgan

learner_material:
SPOKEN MODEL — Complaints And Resolutions

A: I'd like to clarify the procedure because the written instructions seem to give two different options.
B: Which part is unclear?
A: The first section says I should apply online, whereas the final paragraph says I can make an appointment. I don't have reliable internet access, so I'd prefer to speak to someone in person.
B: In that case, you can book an appointment. You'll need to bring identification and the reference letter.
A: So, just to confirm, I don't need to complete the online form first?
B: That's correct. Bring those two documents and explain the situation when you arrive.

A: I'd like to clarify the procedure because the written instructions seem to give two different options.
B: Which part is unclear?
A: The first section says I should apply online, whereas the final paragraph says I can make an appointment. I don't have reliable internet access, so I'd prefer to speak to someone in person.
B: In that case, you can book an appointment. You'll need to bring identification and the reference letter.
A: So, just to confirm, I don't need to complete the online form first?
B: That's correct. Bring those two documents and explain the situation when you arrive.

learner_material:
INFORMATION ARTICLE — Digital Services

A local organisation has reviewed the way it manages digital services. The changes were introduced after users reported that the previous system was difficult to understand and sometimes caused unnecessary delays. From next month, information will be available through both an online service and a staffed reception point.

The organisation says the new arrangements should make the process quicker. However, some users are concerned that people with limited digital access may still need additional support. Staff have therefore been asked to explain the options clearly and to record recurring problems so that the service can be reviewed again after three months.

Anyone affected by the changes is advised to check current guidance before making an appointment.

independent_task: Read the supplied Level 1 text independently. Answer questions on purpose, main ideas, detailed information, vocabulary/context and at least one inference or viewpoint.
success_check: Performance is relevant to R1.6 at Level 1.
Learner handles main meaning, relevant detail and appropriate language with substantial independence.
Tutor records accuracy, independence and a specific next step.
independent_resource:
INDEPENDENT READING — Digital Services

Following a six-week trial, the service has decided to continue its revised arrangements. Most users said that waiting times had improved, although several respondents wanted clearer written instructions. Managers have agreed to rewrite the guidance and provide a telephone option for people who cannot use the online system.

The next review will compare waiting times, complaints and user feedback. If the figures do not improve, further changes may be introduced. Users are encouraged to keep copies of important messages and report difficulties promptly.

key_language: clarify, confirm, whereas, however, therefore, in my view, I suggest, could you explain, just to confirm
learner_material:
SPOKEN MODEL — Planning An Event

A: I'd like to clarify the procedure because the written instructions seem to give two different options.
B: Which part is unclear?
A: The first section says I should apply online, whereas the final paragraph says I can make an appointment. I don't have reliable internet access, so I'd prefer to speak to someone in person.
B: In that case, you can book an appointment. You'll need to bring identification and the reference letter.
A: So, just to confirm, I don't need to complete the online form first?
B: That's correct. Bring those two documents and explain the situation when you arrive.
